question: Among the logged poster inspections in scans.csv, did Iris have a different overall print-inspection warning rate from Juniper?
design: Observational comparison of two devices using the four aggregated shift-by-device rows in scans.csv. The unit of analysis is one logged poster inspection; checked is the denominator and flagged the numerator. The primary comparison is the overall (both shifts combined) warning-rate difference, Iris minus Juniper, with a two-sided Fisher exact test. A prespecified sensitivity analysis stratifies by shift (dawn, dusk) using the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio and the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, because shift may confound device and device allocation was by availability without randomization. No causal device effect is estimated. A falsifying observation would be an overall rate difference whose interval excludes zero, or a stratified association test with p below 0.05.
evaluation: Primary metric: overall warning proportion flagged/checked by device, as a proportion in [0,1]. Report counts, proportions, Wilson intervals, the risk difference with a Newcombe hybrid-score interval, and the two-sided Fisher exact p-value. Sensitivity analysis reports shift-specific proportions, the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio and the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel chi-square p-value. Interpretation uses a two-sided 0.05 level but no threshold-based dichotomization beyond the reported tests. Stopping rule: one deterministic analysis of the complete supplied file, with no additional data or subgroup search.
data_already_inspected: scans.csv (all four rows) and field-note.md were read before this plan was written; these criteria are therefore retrospective, not preregistered. The observed equality of the crude rates motivated the shift-stratified sensitivity criterion.
budget: Local files only. One analysis script using the Python 3 standard library; no network, no installs, no external services and no additional data collection.

criteria.description: Report the total and device-specific checked and flagged counts and warning proportions, with Wilson intervals, as numeric evidence in research/results.csv.
Report the overall risk difference (Iris minus Juniper) with a Newcombe interval and the two-sided Fisher exact p-value from research/tests.csv.
Report shift-specific warning proportions and the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio with the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test p-value as a prespecified sensitivity analysis for shift confounding.
Interpret the outcome and allocation using the primary record: a flag is a print-inspection warning, not a confirmed defect, and devices were assigned by availability without randomization.
